name: Mission-driven threat modelling
description: Maintain a threat model that starts from mission objectives and names an owner for each risk across all segments.
verify: Pick one attack path and confirm the model predicted it, an owner exists and the residual risk was accepted in writing.
references: NASA Space Security Best Practices Guide

name: Supply chain assurance and bills of materials
description: Require software and hardware bills of materials, provenance evidence and security terms from every supplier of flight and ground items.
verify: Trace one flight component and one ground product back to source and show the bill of materials matches what is installed.

name: Security terms for shared and third-party services
description: Contract for isolation, logging, incident notification and exit rights with ground-station, cloud and managed-service providers.
verify: Ask the provider for tenant-isolation evidence and your own audit logs for a named pass; time how long it takes.

name: Mission dependency and trust-boundary map
description: Keep a current map of assets, data flows, radio links and trust boundaries, including those owned by others.
verify: Walk a command from operator console to actuator and check every hop and key appears on the map.

name: Public exposure management
description: Review what filings, papers, job adverts, repositories and internet scans reveal, and remove or accept each item.
verify: Have an outsider build a target pack from public sources in a day and compare it with your own list.

name: Vulnerability management for flight and ground
description: Track vulnerabilities in flight software, ground products and terminals, with a decision for assets that cannot be patched.
verify: Select a recent advisory for a ground product in use and show time to triage, decision and closure.

name: Authenticated telecommand
description: Authenticate every telecommand at the link layer so the spacecraft only acts on frames from a holder of the mission key.
verify: In a lab, send a well-formed but unauthenticated command and confirm it is rejected and reported in telemetry.

name: Link encryption
description: Encrypt telecommand, telemetry and payload links wherever mission and regulation allow, using reviewed algorithms.
verify: Capture a downlink in the lab and confirm no housekeeping or user data is readable without keys.

name: Anti-replay protection
description: Bind commands to counters or time windows so a recorded frame cannot be accepted twice or out of order.
verify: Replay a previously accepted command in the lab and confirm rejection and counter behaviour across a reboot.

name: Key management and on-orbit rekey
description: Generate, store, rotate and revoke keys under hardware protection, with a rehearsed way to rekey spacecraft in orbit.
verify: Rehearse a key compromise: rotate the active key on a flatsat and measure time and operator steps.

name: Signed updates and secure boot
description: Accept only cryptographically signed software, firmware and bitstreams, verified at load and at boot from an immutable root.
verify: Attempt to load an unsigned and a wrongly signed image on a test unit and confirm both are refused and logged.

name: On-board partitioning and least privilege
description: Separate payload, hosted and platform functions so a fault or compromise in one cannot command another.
verify: From the payload interface on a flatsat, try to address platform functions and confirm the bus gateway blocks it.

name: Critical-command authorisation
description: Classify hazardous commands and require independent approval or an arming sequence before they execute.
verify: Try to issue a hazardous command with one operator account and confirm the system demands a second approval.

name: Ground network segmentation
description: Isolate mission operations, station equipment and enterprise IT, with tightly defined and monitored crossings.
verify: From an enterprise workstation, enumerate reachable mission services; the expected answer is none.

name: Strong identity for mission operations
description: Require phishing-resistant multi-factor sign-in, privileged-access workstations and session recording for mission roles.
verify: Review last month's mission-enclave sign-ins for any single-factor, shared or unowned account.

name: Hardened stations, modems and remote access
description: Harden and patch internet-facing appliances, modems, baseband units and antenna controllers; remove default access.
verify: Scan your own address space and station subnets for management interfaces and default credentials.

name: Secure development and toolchain integrity
description: Protect source, build and signing systems; use reviewed changes, reproducible builds and separated signing keys.
verify: Rebuild a released flight image from source on a clean machine and compare hashes with what was flown.

name: Interference-resistant links and navigation
description: Use spreading, hopping, directional antennas, power margin and authenticated navigation signals to resist jamming and spoofing.
verify: Inject calibrated interference in a cabled test and record the margin at which the link or fix is lost.

name: User terminal and fleet-management hardening
description: Sign terminal firmware, isolate the management plane from user traffic and rate-limit fleet-wide actions.
verify: Try to push a configuration to more than a set fraction of test terminals at once and confirm a brake engages.

name: Physical and hardware tamper protection
description: Control physical access to sites and hardware; disable debug ports and design against fault injection where exposure is high.
verify: Inspect a terminal or test unit for live debug interfaces and unattended access routes at a remote site.

name: Cloud tenant isolation and API security
description: Scope cloud and service credentials tightly, rotate them, and verify tenant separation for scheduling, data and keys.
verify: Use a deliberately over-used test credential and confirm it cannot see or schedule another mission's contacts.

name: Data integrity and provenance
description: Sign or seal mission products and operational data such as ephemerides so recipients can detect alteration.
verify: Alter one byte of a test product and an orbit file in staging and confirm downstream consumers reject them.

name: Personnel security and insider-risk programme
description: Vet, train and support staff and contractors; watch for coercion and separate duties for sensitive roles.
verify: Check whether one person could alone change flight software and release it to operations.

name: Authenticated crosslinks and mesh routing
description: Authenticate and authorise inter-satellite traffic so one spacecraft cannot command or reroute its neighbours.
verify: In a constellation simulator, let one node misbehave and confirm neighbours reject its control traffic.

name: Command and telemetry anomaly detection
description: Reconcile commands sent with commands received and check telemetry for physically implausible values and patterns.
verify: Inject an unlogged command in a twin and measure how long before an analyst is alerted.

name: On-board integrity monitoring
description: Monitor memory, tables and execution on board, and report or act on unexpected change.
verify: Modify a table on a flatsat outside the normal procedure and confirm the change is flagged in telemetry.

name: Spectrum monitoring and interference geolocation
description: Monitor carriers and noise floors for unexpected emitters and keep a route to geolocate and report interference.
verify: Introduce a test carrier in a monitored band and time detection, characterisation and escalation.

name: Mission-aware security operations
description: Feed mission control, station and identity logs to analysts who understand space protocols and operations tempo.
verify: Ask the SOC to explain an out-of-window command burst from last month's logs within an hour.

name: Threat intelligence and sector sharing
description: Consume and contribute space-sector threat reporting and act on indicators and warnings.
verify: Trace the last sector advisory received to a concrete change or a recorded decision not to act.

name: Navigation and timing integrity monitoring
description: Cross-check position and time against independent sources and alarm on divergence.
verify: Offset one timing source in a lab and confirm the alarm fires and the system holds over on a trusted source.

name: Space-specific incident response
description: Maintain response plans that cover spacecraft, links and providers, with pre-agreed authority to act during a pass.
verify: Run a timed exercise in which control of one spacecraft is in doubt and record every decision delay.

name: Cyber-aware safe mode
description: Give the spacecraft a minimal, well-protected state that keeps authentication on and can refuse an untrusted ground.
verify: Force safe mode on a flatsat and confirm command authentication, counters and logging remain enforced.

name: Alternate command paths and sites
description: Hold a geographically and administratively separate way to command the spacecraft with its own credentials.
verify: Command a test spacecraft or twin from the alternate site with the primary site declared lost.

name: Trusted recovery of spacecraft software
description: Keep an immutable known-good image and a verified procedure to restore and attest flight software.
verify: Corrupt the active image on a flatsat and restore from the protected image; verify by measurement, not by telemetry alone.

name: Ground backup and rebuild
description: Keep offline, tested backups of mission systems, databases, procedures and key material, and rehearse rebuild.
verify: Rebuild the mission control system from backups on clean hardware and command a simulator.

name: Mission continuity and graceful degradation
description: Design for degraded service: spares, alternative providers, fallback navigation and user communication plans.
verify: Remove one spacecraft, one station or one provider in an exercise and measure service delivered to users.
